           GERANIUM MACULATUM

         Crane's-bill


Habitual sick headaches.   Profuse, hæmorrhages  ,
        pulmonary and from different organs. Vomiting of blood.   Ulceration
        of stomach  .   Atonic and foul ulcers  . Summer
        complaint.



Head.--  Giddiness, with diplopia; better, closing eyes. Ptosis
        and dilated pupils. Sick headache.



Mouth.--  Dry; tip of tongue burning. Pharyngitis.



Stomach.--  Catarrhal gastritis with profuse secretion, tendency
        to ulceration and passive hæmorrhage.   Lessens the vomiting in
        gastric ulcer  .



Stool.--  Constant desire to go to stool, with inability to pass
        anything for some time. Chronic diarrhœa, with offensive mucus. Constipation.



Female.--  Menses too profuse. Post-partum hæmorrhage. Sore
        nipples (  Eup arom  ).



Relationship.--  Compare:   Geranin
        1x. Constant hawking and spitting in elderly people.   Erodium  -Hemlock-Stork's
        bill--(a popular hæmostatic in Russia, and especially used for metrorrhagia and
        menorrhagia);   Hydrastinin; Cinch; Sabin  .



Dose.--  Tincture, half-dram doses in gastric ulcer. Tincture,
        to third attenuation, as a general rule. Locally, in ulcers, it will destroy the pyogenic
        membrane.
